title: rust-oscore 0.1.3: separate response-replay window from request-PIV reuse record (two-window design)
description: ADJUDICATED (Mark, 2026-08-30): approve the two-window separation design for the rust-oscore observe port. Root cause (project-LICHEN-worker6-xhnx, same root as ythw): response_seq/response_window is written by mark_response_used only from protect_response's no-PIV branch (SERVER role: request PIVs whose nonces were reused for no-PIV responses) but consulted by begin_unprotect_response_inner (CLIENT role: peer response PIVs accepted). One window, two unrelated sequence spaces: on a bidirectional context, legitimate notifications whose PIV falls in the server-reuse range are falsely rejected (fail-close of valid traffic), while client-side notification replay was previously a no-op (ythw). DESIGN: split into two distinct persisted state structures per context: (1) response_replay_window — client role, consulted by begin_unprotect_response_inner / begin_unprotect_observe_response, records peer response PIVs accepted; (2) request_piv_reuse_record — server role, written by mark_response_used, consulted by protect_response's no-PIV branch to prevent double-reuse of a request nonce. Each role consults ONLY its own window. Both windows persist per-context through the 0.1.2 persistence machinery (versioned authenticated records — the 0.1.2 format version bumps for the new fields). SCOPE: rust-oscore crate internals (human-bar work, Mark or dedicated reviewed pass — not fleet work). RELEASE: oscore 0.1.3 -> LICHEN bumps the registry dep -> 3exb (notification-replay test) lands with it -> lichen-node gateway-union build verified. Sequenced with the LICHEN fleet offline for that window (workers pause while the dep bumps). Acceptance: (a) ythw scenario — replayed notification rejected; (b) xhnx scenario — bidirectional context, notification PIV numerically inside server-reuse range is ACCEPTED; (c) server double-reuse of a request nonce still rejected; (d) persistence round-trip across restart carries both windows; (e) all existing oscore/observe tests green.
